<!-- pr-reviewer: b1335bd77ebcb9b7a3fcf28bb1d6761f4c10f4d9 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

**What looks good**
- Clean-room: dual contouring is cited to Ju/Losasso/Schaefer/Warren (SIGGRAPH 2002) and the Jacobi solver to Golub & Van Loan, in every new module's provenance line. The normal/trust estimators are described honestly as our own (`hermite.rs` header and `docs/decisions/23-dual-contouring.md` say they are not from the paper and record the measured 0.35-cell failure of plain gradients).
- Prime Directive: no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new non-test code. `Grid::val` is bounds-checked and returns NaN off the lattice. `qef::solve` clamps the vertex into its cell, and a non-finite answer falls back to the mass point. Singular values under 0.1 of the largest are truncated. The Jacobi loop is capped at 32 sweeps. `iso::extract_with` never returns a dual mesh with an open edge: it logs and serves the marching mesh instead.
- All new files are under 400 lines (dual 248, hermite 208, qef 166, iso 293). The PR has a decision file, a `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #23`, a conventional subject, and no CHANGELOG.md edit. There are no dependency, build.rs, `.github` or script changes.

**Local results (merged with current origin/main; the trial merge was clean)**
| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` (lib 62 plus all 24 integration suites incl. `stock_dual` 5/5) | all pass |
| `camcraft-app --test stock_export` | 2/2 |
| `camcraft-ui --lib machined` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 2/2 |
| `camcraft-ui --test gpu_render machined_mesh_paints_as_stock` | 1/1 (runs headless) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Adversarial probe (a throwaway test, not committed, deleted afterwards):
- A 1-cell-thick wall extracted closed with finite triangles. Dual volume was 99.86 against marching's 93.3 (true value 100).
- A 1.3-cell wall off the lattice and a pocket pair that leaves a thin web between them were also closed under both methods.
- Sub-cell features (a 0.3-thick plate, a 0.05 sliver) extract as an empty mesh under both methods, with no error and no panic. That is a sampling limit shared with marching, not a regression.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. Ball-pocket volume: dual is 949.8 and marching 948.0 against 957.5 exact. The shortfall is the same for both, so it is not caused by this PR. Dual is slightly closer, and the pinning test asserts it is no worse than marching. It most likely comes from the field's cell-centre sampling of the curved surface. I would leave it as a follow-up issue rather than block on it.
2. The open-edge fallback logs with `eprintln!`, as the rest of this module does. It is not visible in the UI, so a silent switch to marching only shows on stderr. Fine for now.
3. Thin features under a cell vanish, as with marching. A future note in the stock-mesh docs may be worth it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
